predecessors.name: Warring States Japan
predecessors.text: the Mōri home domain around Yoshida-Kōriyama in Aki

ledger.x: 1523: Kōmatsumaru died; 'The senior Mōri vassals met and decided to offer the leadership to Motonari' (10 August entry to Yoshida-Kōriyama).
By 1550: the clan page says Motonari 'expanded the clan's power across Aki'; he beat Takeda Motoshige at Arita-Nakaide in 1517.
By 1550: 'Motonari had Bingo Province, with the Kobayakawa clan supporting him' (the page gives no event year).
Around 1550: 'Motonari held Iwami Province with the Kikkawa clan'; in 1556 Amago Haruhisa captured Yamabuki Castle and the Iwami silver mine.
1557: 'it would take the Mōri until 1557 to force Ōuchi Yoshinaga to commit suicide and years longer to completely bring Suo province and Nagato province under Mōri's control'.
1558: 'Mōri captured Moji castle from the Ōuchi.'
1558: the Moji front against Ōtomo Sōrin begins (the page: Sōrin retook the castle in September 1559; an Ōtomo assault failed in 1561).
1562: 'Motonari invaded Izumo', beginning the second siege of Toda Castle (1562-1563); 'Amago Yoshihisa later surrendered'.
1566: 'The Amago clan, the Mōri's traditional rival, had been destroyed' (Terumoto page); in 1570 Amago Katsuhisa was beaten at Fubeyama and fled to Oki.
1566: the Amago destroyed.
1569: Ōuchi Teruhiro's rebellion beaten in October; 'The Mōri lost influence in Chikuzen and most Buzen bases'; the Sōrin page: Tatarahama 1569, Tachibana castle retaken by the Ōtomo.
October 1569: 'most Buzen bases' lost.
1571: the lands 'stretched from Buzen on Kyushu to the borders of Harima and Bizen'.
1576-1578: the Mōri intervened in the Ishiyama Hongan-ji War (First Battle of Kizugawaguchi, 1576); 'Kōzuki Castle in Harima was besieged' in 1577-1578; the Honganji surrendered in 1580.
1582: Hideyoshi besieged Takamatsu Castle in Bitchū; 'After Honnōji, the Mōri made peace with Hideyoshi'; the page lists no lands ceded.
1589: Terumoto is 'Lord of Hiroshima' 1589-1600 (succession table); the page says he built Hiroshima Castle and gives no date.
1600: 'After Sekigahara, Ieyasu reduced his domains, leaving him only Nagato and Suō Provinces, worth 369,000 koku in total'; Terumoto had nominally led the Western Army (clan page).
1600: Chōshū Domain 'established', based at Hagi Castle in Nagato; the clan's holdings cut from 1,200,000 to 369,000 koku.
1600: the capital moves from Hiroshima to Hagi (clan page; Chōshū page: based at Hagi Castle in Nagato).
1862: 'Hagi Castle's status as capital ended, and Yamaguchi Castle became the capital (1862-1871).'
1871: 'the han system was abolished, and the domain's territory was absorbed into Yamaguchi Prefecture.'

wars.name: Battle of Miyajima (Itsukushima)
wars.outcome: Motonari sailed out on 1 October 1555 in a thunderstorm; Ōuchi Yoshinaga was forced to suicide in 1557.

wars.name: Mōri conquest of Suō and Nagato
wars.outcome: Yoshinaga's suicide in 1557; years more to bring Suō and Nagato fully under control (no year on the page).

wars.name: Mōri–Ōtomo war in Buzen
wars.outcome: Moji changed hands in 1558-1559; the Mōri lost most Buzen bases in 1569.

wars.name: Mōri conquest of Izumo
wars.outcome: The Toda siege of 1562-1563; the Amago destroyed by 1566; Katsuhisa beaten at Fubeyama in 1570 and fled to Oki.

wars.name: Chūgoku campaign against the Mōri
wars.outcome: Takamatsu was besieged in 1582; the Mōri made peace with Hideyoshi after Honnōji and became his vassals in 1583.

wars.name: Sekigahara campaign (Mōri side)
wars.outcome: Terumoto nominally led the Western Army, which lost; the Mōri were cut to Nagato and Suō.

wars.name: Boshin War (Chōshū side)
wars.outcome: The Chōshū army used a flag during the war (page); the pages give no start or end year or battles.

certainty.note: The pages name castles, provinces and koku, not borders; the Chūgoku provinces are drawn as prefectures with circles for Aki's core and Bitchū.
